title: Stress-driven spatial patterning may be conserved across bacteria, metazoa and models

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stress-driven spatial patterning may be conserved across bacteria, metazoa and models

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Noting that oscillatory nitrogen stress responses pattern bacterial biofilms and that stress responses define stripe regions in their simulated tissue, the authors suggest that conserved stress-based dynamics could underlie the scaling of spatial patterning from single-cell metabolic goals in bacteria, metazoans and minimal in silico models, similar to the clock-and-wavefront model of somitogenesis.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, conserved dynamics could be relevant across bacterial, metazoan and in silico minimal models of the scaling of spatial patterning from single-cell metabolic and stress dynamics.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Discussion”. Scope: Bacterial biofilms, metazoan segmentation, in silico tissue models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public studies can support comparisons of selected systems, and the simulation is reproducible. The sweeping conservation claim needs harmonized cross-system data and phylogenetic or mechanistic evidence that current datasets do not provide.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define common dynamical signatures such as stress oscillation period, propagation, phase coupling, and boundary formation, then compare time series from bacterial biofilms, metazoan segmentation, and the model. Conservation requires homologous or mechanistically equivalent stress circuitry plus shared dynamics beyond generic oscillation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The taxonomic scope is much broader than available matched time series.

Similar oscillations can arise from unrelated mechanisms.

Stress and pattern boundaries are measured differently across systems.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pieces of the comparison are public: segmentation-clock models and expression series, and the tissue simulation. They can test a restricted dynamical resemblance. They do not contain a cross-kingdom homology or a matched stress-to-pattern experiment, so the conservation reading stays underdetermined.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare published bacterial biofilm stress oscillations, vertebrate segmentation-clock time series, and stress-linked stripe formation in the French-flag model for a shared motif in which a metabolic or stress oscillation sets spatial boundaries. A common motif under a pre-specified distance on those series would support a shared dynamical pattern; qualitatively different mechanisms would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No single public dataset pairs biofilm nitrogen stress, vertebrate segmentation, and the neural cellular automaton under one schema.

Shared oscillation-plus-pattern is compatible with analogy and does not show a conserved mechanism from bacteria to metazoans.
